A yacht on blue water beside a small inflatable boat

Days 4–10 are spent around the Antarctic Peninsula and sailing south towards the Antarctic Circle. In late Antarctic summer, humpback whales feed on krill before migrating north. The penguin chicks are old enough to head to sea, and leopard seals hunt near the shore. All the sites below are possible stops during this period. The expedition team decides the exact order.

At Hannah Point on Livingston Island, you may see gentoo and chinstrap penguins, southern giant petrels and elephant seals. Deception Island is a volcanic caldera that opens to the sea, forming a natural harbour. An abandoned whaling station still stands at Whalers Bay. Cape petrels, gulls, brown and south polar skuas, and Antarctic terns are found here. Wilson’s and black-bellied storm petrels nest among the old structures.

Small, steep Cuverville Island, between the mountains of the peninsula and Rongé Island, is home to a large gentoo penguin colony and nesting brown skuas. At Neko Harbour, possible activities include Zodiac trips with views of glaciers and peaks and a landing on the Antarctic mainland. At Paradise Bay, a Zodiac cruise may offer sightings of humpback and minke whales.

If the ice allows, the ship sails through the Lemaire Channel to Pléneau and Petermann islands. You can look for Adélie penguins and blue-eyed Antarctic shags, and may also spot humpback whales, minke whales and leopard seals. The route then continues south past the Argentine Islands to Crystal Sound, where a morning crossing of the Antarctic Circle is planned if ice conditions are suitable.

On Detaille Island, a landing may be possible at an abandoned British research station surrounded by high mountains and glaciers. On the way north, the Fish Islands offer a chance to see one of the more southerly colonies of Adélie penguins and Antarctic shags in this part of the peninsula. Icebergs are plentiful around the Melchior Islands, where leopard seals, fur seals and whales occur. The area is also listed as a possible dive site. Participation, conditions and cost are confirmed separately. Conditions in the Drake Passage determine when the ship sets out on the return crossing.
